newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Part-time Australian bowler Michael Bevan made up for his comparative failure with the bat yesterday by taking 3-46 in the West Indies second innings to help spin Australia to victory over the Windies in the first Test in Brisbane. Page 1.

Australian tennis champion Evonne Cawley believes Australia is on the threshold of producing another world champion. Despite this prediction, Cawley says the reason behind the demise of Australia's women on the tennis circuit could be Tennis Queensland's three-year break from a women's tournament. Page 23.

Australia's Kenyan long-distance runner Luke Kipkosgei could be the next to translate his strong form during the Australian domestic season into success the following European term. Kipkosgei broke the great runner Henry Rono's record for the fastest 10,00m on Australian soil. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby League club North Sydney refused to join the rebel competition Superleague because of six key points, one of which was the fear the team would end in limbo. The Bears revealed the Optus offer was more attractive than that offered by Superleague and decided to stay with the original competition. Page 45.

Two Australian runners Shaun Creighton and Darren Wilson have broken Ron Clarke's Australian record for the 10,000m. Originally set by running sensation Ron Clarke, the two youngsters ran a speedy pace at 27:31.92 and 27:37.00 respectively. Page 45.

A squad of 13 cricketers was named yesterday for the second Test despite selectors deferring the naming of the final twelve until they have ascertained the state of the pitch. South Australian cricketers Greg Blewett and Peter McIntyre have been recalled to Test duties. Page 45.
THE AGE

According to a surprising report released this week, one in five Australian athletes do not believe taking banned drugs is cheating. However, the Australian Sports Drug Agency report revealed these athletes were deterred from using drugs by drug testing pograms. Page C16.

Australian basketballer Luc Longley severely dislocated his shoulder yesterday after a wave sent him crashing into a sandbar when swimming at a beach in California. With other Chicago Bulls players injured, the news has come at a particularly bad time. Pae C16.

The Victorian Bushrangers invited golfer Greg Norman to a training session at the MCG yesterday in their preparation for the Sheffield Shield match against Queensland. The Victorians fly to Brisbane this morning with the four-day game starting on Friday. age C15.
HERALD SUN

Australian golfer Greg Norman reassured fans yesterday that his degenerating back ailment was not a threat to his career. Norman, who was recently crowned Australian Open champion, plans to take a break from the sport after his own tournament here this wek. Page 72.

Golfer Frank Nobilo has withdrawn from the Holden Classic following a cancer scare. Nobilo thought he had cancer in the shoulders after feeling incredible pain, but was diagnosed with torn and inflamed tendons. Page 73.

The classic wheelrace Forges will make a comeback in Victoria next year. The race will be part of the Australian Madison program on March 1 1997, making it one of the country's richest carnivals with A$20,000 in prize money on offer. Page 71.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The art of curling is currently on display in Sydney. The Pacific Curling Championships started last night at the Canterbury Ice Rink, with Australian competitors aiming for a spot on the 1998 Winter Olympic program. Page 78.

The Australian Baseball Federation look set to clash with New South Wales Olympics Minister Michael Knight over the Olympic venue. Baseball officials are not happy with the site, claiming it is below the minimum requirements for their sport. Page 78.

Wallaby coach Greg Smith has demanded an explanation from critics who say he should be sacked. Smith defended his performance during his first year of rugby union coaching and believes any criticism is unwarranted. It has been revealed there is a push to have Smith replaced midway through his two-year term. Page 78.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
